newsitem.title: USA: CIGNA unit settles class action suit.
newsitem.headline: CIGNA unit settles class action suit.

text.p: CIGNA Corp subsidiary Connecticut General Life Insurance Co said on Friday it settled a class action lawsuit with individuals whose policies were affected by increased taxes on life insurers and declining interest rates.
The company said it provided them with a variety of options and benefits, but that the settlement would not have a material effect on its earnings or financial position.
Connecticut General said the settlement did not represent an admission of guilt and no court had found it at fault.
The settlement covered 130,000 Connecticut General clients who bought whole life, universal life or participating whole life products between August 1, 1983 and March 26, 1996.
The unit said it decided to settle to avoid legal costs.
Clients' products had been affected by the Deferred Acquisition Cost Legislation of 1990, which taxed life insurers, the CIGNA said.
Connecticut General said these clients would receive an adjustment in future years and some would have the option to buy a fixed annuity with a one-time enhancement.
